<reason>B wins by exposing the missing justification for additional liability beyond companies’ own negligence. A credibly identifies preventive tools, particularly reliable plaza geofencing, but does not establish why existing fault-based duties cannot address unreasonable failures to use them. Its sweeping claims that almost nothing is tried and omissions are always excusable remain unsupported. B also shows that A’s reasonable-safeguards exception leaves its vanished-rider compensation problem unresolved, while directly answering both pressure questions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B accepts liability for negligently omitting reliable geofencing, neutralizing A’s strongest pressure question. It then uses A’s concession that liability should fade after reasonable safeguards to demand the unanswered distinction between the proposed higher duty and ordinary negligence.</best_rebuttal>
